posts.title: Always Burning: 150 Years of the Carlsberg Research Laboratory
posts.description: This piece is shortlisted for Best Commissioned Beer Writing at the British Guild of Beer Writers Awards 2026, so it seemed a good moment to set it free from behind the paywall. It first appeared in Brewer and Distiller International in January/February 2026, and my thanks go to Steve and the team there for commissioning it and for letting me share it here. Photo: Carlsberg Group / Daniel Urhøj Andersen We explore how this scientific powerhouse continues to prioritise global progress over proprietary profit. As we step inside the Carlsberg Research Laboratory, which celebrated its 150th anniversary in 2025, we remember its unique foundation structure – and that this was the facility that gave the brewing world pure yeast and the pH scale – as well as Zoran Gojkovic’s boundary-pushing experiments with climate-resilient grains. posts.title: Go on, tell me how you really feel
posts.description: Trust me, bruh, you’re about to read some real S-tier writing. Ugh. What does S-tier mean? How is an S higher than an A? And why should I care? You’ve seen the videos. Some geezer, mouth hanging open in the thumbnail, drones on as he drags multitools or crisp flavours or TV shows from the 1970s and ’80s into rows marked S, A, B, C, D, sometimes even down through E and F to G. Yet never do our pop-culture megaminds, our consumer-goods sleuths, think to explain what separates one tier from another. I mean, my god. Scoring things. Ranking them. Rating them. Happens all the time. This isn’t a post about how those reviews and ratings on that air fryer you’re about to order are probably maybe absolutely fake. It’s more that it wouldn’t matter if they were real anyway. If there’s no way to know what separates a three-star rating from a four-star one, both are basically meaningless. posts.title: A greener spirit: the rise of sustainable English whisky
posts.description: This feature ran in the July/August 2025 issue of Brewer and Distiller International, the journal of the Chartered Institute of Brewers and Distillers. I wanted to know whether English whisky, still young enough to be working out what it is, could make sustainability part of its identity from the start. What I found was a sector heading in broadly the same direction while disagreeing, sometimes sharply, about how to get there. Since publication: The English whisky GI came into force on 1 October 2026, though it has since faced appeals. Ellers Farm's first whisky is due for release tomomrrow, 23 October 2026. There's no public sign yet of the EWG's sustainability roadmap; the GI seems to have taken up most of the Guild's attention for now.
